transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-12-06 15:00 UTC | Duration: 62m | Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Elena Morris (Redwood SE), Lara Chen (Cadenza Procurement), Omar Ruiz (Cadenza Legal), Priya Nair (Cadenza Eng)

Summary: Quick procurement review - MSA and DPA status, SLAs for Dedicated vs Hosted, pricing approvers and PO timeline, onboarding steps for pilot (benchmarks + runbook). Shared artifacts: redwood/msas/2026-10-redwood-msa.pdf (sent), redwood/dpa/redline-2026-12-06.pdf (link), pilot-benchmark-template.xlsx (Elena link)

Topics: MSA redlines; DPA data residency and subprocessors; SLAs (uptime, latency p95); pricing approval gates; private vs dedicated deployment; pilot scope and success criteria; onboarding timeline

Action items recap at end.

Transcript:
00:00 Samir: All right everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Samir from Redwood A-E, and with me is Elena from our SE team. How's everybody doing?
00:07 Lara: Hi Samir, hi Elena. Good thanks. Quick note, we have Omar and Priya on too - we wanted to make sure legal and eng are aligned today.
00:14 Samir: Perfect. The goal for today is to walk through the current MSA/DPA redlines, align on SLA asks for the contract, and map the onboarding pilot steps and timing. We'll keep it to an hour but obviously run over if needed.
00:26 Elena: And I'll pick up the technical bits - pilot runbook, benchmarking expectations, VPC options, things like K-V cache and how the KV cache is handled on Dedicated. I might stumble on pronouncing things, sorry - I say KV cache a lot.
00:42 Omar: Great. Starting with MSA, Omar here. We sent a handful of redlines - mainly around indemnity, liability caps, and termination for cause. We also want to ensure data processing boundaries in the DPA are explicit, especially around sub processors.
00:56 Samir: Understood. We reviewed your redline doc - thanks, very thorough. On liability caps we typically standardize to X monthly or Y contract value, but we can run the numbers with finance. For DPA, our standard includes subprocessors list and we can add an audit clause. Any specific regs you need for data residency? E.g., EU-only, or specific APAC sites?
01:15 Lara: For Cadenza Retail, PCI scope is limited, but we do want EU customer data to remain in EU for the pilot and production. Is Redwood able to guarantee region pinning for Hosted or do we need Dedicated?
01:28 Elena: For region pinning we offer routing policies - for strict residency we recommend Dedicated or our Private VPC option. Hosted can be region-aware but isn't guaranteed isolation at the hardware level. There's sometimes confusion with the public-hosted regions versus dedicated pools.
01:42 Priya: To clarify from an engineering POV, our main requirements are: 1) p95 latency below 300ms for short prompts, 2) ability to run a nightly batch of 10M tokens with cost caps, and 3) audit logs for all requests for three years. On logs - we need immutable audit trail (not just metrics) and SSO integration.
02:00 Elena: Right. SSO/SAML support is already in our control plane, we support SAML and OIDC. Audit logs can be exported to your SIEM via syslog or S3 with separate ledgering. For immutability we recommend using your own S3 with object lock, or we can provide signed audit streams. I know our legal docs reference audit logs but I'll attach a tech note.
02:17 Omar: On encryption, we need keys under our control. Does Redwood support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM)? Also, we want the ability to rotate without downtime.
02:26 Samir: Yes, we support KMS integration for Private and Dedicated. For Hosted, you can use our KMS integration but note that Hosted has some multi-tenant control plane elements. Rotation is supported - we have rolling key rotations that don't require downtime for KV cache, but I'll have Elena detail that in the runbook.
02:42 Priya: When you say 'KV cache' earlier, we've seen in other vendors that the KV cache can leak prefixes across requests. Need assurance there.
02:49 Elena: We do per-tenant KV isolation on Dedicated and Private. On Hosted, we do logical isolation; there are protections but if you require hardware isolation that is Dedicated. Also note quantization profiles and kernel selection affect throughput - can impact your nightly batch cost.
03:05 Lara: Let's talk SLAs - we asked for 99.95 uptime and 50ms median latency guarantees for hosted endpoints. That's aggressive. What can you commit in MSA?
03:16 Samir: For Hosted tier we normally commit 99.9 uptime with best-effort latency targets. For Dedicated we offer SLA up to 99.95 with financial credits. For p95 latency SLOs we usually publish targets in the console - but contractual p95 latency guarantees are part of enterprise tier and depend on committed capacity. We can include an SLA exhibit in the MSA for Dedicated.
03:34 Omar: And remedies - credits vs termination rights? We need clarity in the MSA on remedies for repeated SLA misses. Also escalation path - who at Redwood is on-call?
03:43 Samir: We can include an escalation matrix in the SLA exhibit and define credit tiers. Termination for repeated SLA breaches can be scoped to material breach after N failures in a rolling 90-day window. We'll propose wording; please highlight anything you want changed in the redline.
03:59 Priya: Pricing approvals - procurement asks: what pricing model will we present for the PO? We need committed spend numbers so finance can sign off. Also do you support monthly commit vs annual?
04:10 Samir: For Dedicated we have monthly and annual commitments; discounts scale with term and committed throughput. For Hosted it's usage-based. For the pilot we can set a short-term committed pool to guarantee baseline latency for your test. I'll send a pricing deck with sample TCO comparisons - we have a pricing sheet that shows tokens, embeddings, and dedicated pool cost.
04:29 Lara: Can you send a sample PO invoice and SOW template? Procurement wants to see standard PO language and invoice cadence.
04:36 Samir: Yes, will attach. I'll also include our purchasing contact and bank details. We typically accept NET30 for enterprise, but we can negotiate NET45 if needed.
04:46 Omar: Back to the DPA - subprocessors list. We need a clause that Redwood will notify changes 30 days in advance and allow us to object and require mitigation.
04:54 Elena: We already have that in the DPA template - notification window and opt-out/mitigation clause. I'll point to the relevant section in the doc and highlight the paragraph in the redline.
05:03 Priya: For the pilot, what is the minimal onboarding time? We have a holiday push in early Jan so want pilot completed by end of Jan. How long from PO to pilot start?
05:13 Samir: For Dedicated pools it's typically 3-6 weeks after PO and account setup, depending on capacity. For Hosted pilot it's immediate with an onboarding call and sample keys. Since you want end of Jan, if we lock a PO this month we can do Hosted pilot ASAP or Dedicated pilot if you accept a 3-4 week provisioning lead time.
05:33 Lara: Our preference is Dedicated for the pilot due to EU data residency. Is there an expedited provisioning path?
05:39 Elena: We do have a rapid-provision program for certain customers - need final capacity commit and a provisioning fee. We can try to accelerate to 2 weeks if capacity is available, but I'll flag capacity with infra ops after this call.
05:51 Omar: On indemnity, can we add carveouts for downstream data processors? We want Redwood to be responsible only for Redwood-controlled subprocessors.
05:59 Samir: Typical carveouts are acceptable. We'll propose language that bounds Redwood responsibility to our direct actions and subcontractors we control. We'll avoid broad indemnities for customer data misuse.
06:10 Priya: Benchmarks - Elena, can you walk through the benchmark plan briefly? What do you need from our side?
06:18 Elena: Sure. We'll run three workload profiles: short-chat prompts, long-document summarization, and nightly bulk embedding. For each we need sample prompt types, 1k example records for latency tests, and a subset of sanitized data for quality checks. We'll measure p50/p95/p99 latencies, tokens/sec throughput, and cost per 1M tokens. Also we'll validate quantization impacts on output fidelity.
06:41 Priya: For the sanitized data, do you need raw PII removed or can we use token-mapped placeholders? We can't share customer PII.
06:49 Elena: Token-mapped placeholders are fine - we only need representative lengths and distribution. Also include a sample of worst-case long context threads.
06:56 Lara: Questions from procurement: what are onboarding fees, support hours included, and who signs the SOW? We need to model these expenses.
07:06 Samir: Onboarding fee depends on Dedicated size; small pools have a one-time setup fee, included support hours vary by tier. We'll include a concise SOW template showing included support hours, training sessions, and premium SLA pricing for enterprise tier.
07:22 Omar: Legal asks that we include an audit right clause for security reviews yearly and a penalty if undisclosed sub processors are added. Also, Cadenza needs breach notification within 24 hours.
07:33 Samir: Our standard breach notification is 72 hours for security incidents, but we can commit to 24 hours for incidents impacting regulated data if required. I'll flag that as negotiable in the MSA redline.
07:47 Priya: One more technical: do you support offline air-gapped inference for PII-heavy pipelines? We might need an on-prem or air-gapped option.
07:56 Elena: We offer a Private on-prem package but that is a separate licensing model. It supports air-gapped deployments and customer-managed infra. We can add an appendix to the SOW if you want to pursue that.
08:08 Samir: Ok, let's do a quick walkthrough of the DPA redline that Omar sent. (Samir shared screen - link: redwood/dpa/redline-2026-12-06.pdf)
08:18 Omar: In section 4, data residency - we want stronger language. The current phrasing allows processing 'within the EU or equivalent', but that's a bit vague for our compliance team.
08:26 Samir: We can narrow that to 'within the EU/EEA or in data centers contracted in EU territories' and add a subprocessors list that is EU-only for Cadenza's production tenant. That will require Dedicated.
08:37 Lara: Fine. Also in the DPA we need the deletion/return of data clause to specify timelines - e.g., data returned within 60 days and verified destruction on all backups within 120 days.
08:49 Samir: We can commit to return within 60 days and deletion within 120 for Dedicated. For Hosted we may need additional language about multi-tenant backups but will propose a reasonable timeline.
09:00 Priya: Any caveats about model fine-tuning or customer data being used to improve models? We need certainty that we opt out.
09:07 Elena: We have an explicit opt-out for model training - customer data is not used for model training unless there's an opt-in. We'll add that clause to the DPA and highlight it for legal.
09:15 Omar: Regarding export controls and data transfer mechanisms - do you rely on standard contractual clauses or other mechanisms?
09:21 Samir: For EU transfers we can use SCCs and we also support data residency to avoid transfers. For any special requests we can coordinate with our privacy team.
09:30 Lara: Let's go over the procurement timeline: we need legal and procurement approvals by 2026-12-20 to make Jan pilot realistic. Omar, is that feasible from legal?
09:39 Omar: We can aim for that if Redwood gets back with MSA/DPA redline and final pricing by 2026-12-10. Otherwise the review could slip into Jan.
09:48 Samir: That's doable - I'll send the annotated MSA and the DPA redline today, and Elena will push the benchmark materials.
09:56 Elena: I'll follow up with a pilot runbook, a shared spreadsheet for benchmarking, and a checklist for sample artifacts. Also I'll propose three pilot SLOs for you to confirm.
10:06 Priya: For success criteria let's list them now: p95 latency <300ms for chat, embedding throughput >10k/sec for nightly batch, and no production-level security findings in the audit.
10:18 Samir: I'll include those as pilot success criteria in the SOW draft.
10:25 Lara: One procurement nuance - we use a standard PO flow and need a contract file name to match our systems. Can you confirm what the SOW filename will be? Procurement wants SOW_Cadenza_2026-12.
10:39 Samir: Yes we can name it that. I'll make sure the SOW and invoice templates have the exact naming convention.
10:47 Omar: A few small misc items - are you SOC 2 and ISO certified? We need cert copies.
10:53 Samir: Yes SOC2 Type II and ISO27001. I'll attach certs with the MSA package.
11:00 Priya: Do you have a product roadmap item about model upgrades and how rollouts are controlled? We don't want silent model changes that affect outputs.
11:07 Elena: We have a rollout policy - canary and A/B rollout with automatic fallback. We also provide version pinning so you can pin to a model build. We'll add this to the runbook and show how to pin and how rollbacks work.
11:19 Lara: Any competitor questions - procurement asked if you have price matching vs competitors. Are you open to a discounted rate if we present a competitor offer?
11:27 Samir: We can consider competitive adjustments if there's a comparable offer - we'll need the competitor proposal and volume to evaluate. We try to be competitive with Bedrock and Anthropic alternatives.
11:36 Omar: Last legal question: data breach insurance and limits. We need to see your insurance certificates and confirm limits.
11:42 Samir: I'll include insurance certs. We carry cyber insurance and can provide the carrier and policy limits.
11:48 Elena: Quick technical note - for the benchmark we'll include both quantized and non-quantized runs to show perf/cost tradeoff; that helps engineering pick the right profile.
11:58 Lara: OK - recap please and next steps.
12:03 Samir: Recap: We'll send annotated MSA and DPA redlines (Samir, today), attach SOC2/ISO and insurance certs (Samir), Elena will send pilot runbook and benchmark template (Elena, by 2026-12-13), Cadenza to provide approver list and sample sanitized data (Priya, by 2026-12-09), Omar to review DPA redlines and return comments (Omar, by 2026-12-14). Procurement to confirm PO process and desired invoice cadence (Lara, by 2026-12-10). Goal: finalize legal and pricing by 2026-12-20 to start pilot before end of January.
12:24 Lara: That works. Thank you. We'll review the docs and get back.
12:28 Samir: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the package and schedule the pilot kickoff after redlines are resolved.
12:34 Meeting end.

Notes on transcript quality: automated transcript had occasional mis-hearings ("sammel" instead of SAML, "KV cash" instead of KV cache). Action items in this export were manually reviewed.
